method_note: Read the whole target. Chose claims with highest oracle impact: spec versions and release dates, IDTA-01002/01001/01004/01005 mechanisms (paths, profile ids, status codes, JWS header, linkset), template semanticIds, IANA registrations, repository licences and activity, all 24 DOIs, and existing_check mappings. Re-fetched IDTA spec sources at tag v3.2.0 and the template JSON through gh api, IANA, Crossref, PyPI and the engine source. EUR-Lex returned empty pages, so law claims were compared only with the repository records. No EN/ISO/IEC/DIN document was opened; IDTA annex text that cites ENs was read only for IDTA's own statements.

rule5_findings.problem: Lists the granularity values Model, Item, Batch as 'DppMetadata granularity values'. IDTA-01001 v3.2 annex labels this value set as EN 18223 granularity, so the sentence reproduces an enumeration of an EN document. The 02099-1 JSON template carries only the example 'Item' and no enumeration.
rule5_findings.fix: Say: 'IDTA-01001 v3.2 maps the DppMetadata granularity string to AssetKind Instance, Type or Batch (annex mapping table); the permitted granularity strings are not recorded here'. Or cite the IDTA table by name as secondary and keep it out of oracle text.

rule5_findings.problem: No violation found. Watch item: the IDTA DPP annexes are themselves organized around EN 18222 operation names, EN clause and table numbers. The file avoids them (scope_note says so) and none appeared in the text. Keep that fence when the engine oracles are written.
rule5_findings.fix: No change. When implementing aas.dpp_compose, cite 'IDTA-01002 v3.2 annex DPP' only and do not copy its EN-labelled operation or clause references.

missed_items.fact: The Technical Data battery template (02035-4, folder 1/0/2) carries administration templateId 'IDTA-02003-2-0', the id of a different IDTA template, unlike its siblings that use https://admin-shell.io/idta-02035-N. Relevant for template-conformance checks that match templateId.

The annex says a DPP document must validate against at least two kinds of schema: a generic DPP schema derived from the CEN data-model standard and the schemas of each content submodel. This supports two separate engine steps (data.jsonschema for the header, template conformance for content).

missed_items.topic: IDTA-01001 v3.2 conformance note on nesting
missed_items.fact: The V3.2 changelog states that a minimum container recursion depth of 32 should be supported and that for certification at most 32 recursion test cases are to be tested. The file records the depth but not the certification hint, which a test oracle can reuse.
admin-shell-io/aas-specs-security was pushed on 2026-10-14, after tag v3.1.0 (2026-07-21); the file does not record post-release activity for this repository, although it does for aas-specs-api.
Besides aas-core3.0-testgen, the org eclipse-aascw also archived aas-core3.0rc02-testgen and aas-core3.1-testgen on 2026-05-12. The file says only that testdatagen succeeds the 3.0 generator.

IDTA-01002 v3.2 prose table shows Limit as nonNegativeInteger with default 100; file's anomaly says prose gives default 100 and schema minimum 1. Both are true; a limit=0 probe is therefore a boundary case worth a fixture.

overall: The target file is highly reliable on the points checked: all 20+ spec, repository, licence, version, date, IANA and engine-mapping claims matched the primary sources, and all 23 Crossref DOIs match title, year and venue. No claim was refuted. Open weaknesses are limited: law paraphrases and the 2026/1778 act rest on 2026-10-13 records because EUR-Lex was empty, the arXiv author count and the EN 18219 catalogue URL are unconfirmed, and one sentence lists a granularity value set labelled by IDTA as EN 18223 content. The file's own anomaly list (profile numbering, assetIds spelling, limit default) is accurate and useful for oracle design.
